title: Why a hook, and where it stops
lede: Inspecting a coding agent otherwise means terminating TLS. A hook avoids it but only covers agents it is installed into. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

only what policy allowed can leave

steps.title: The usual way to inspect an agent
steps.what: Terminate TLS: install a certificate on every developer machine and write a decryption policy for the traffic.

steps.title: What that costs
steps.what: A proxy that decrypts everything, a certificate to distribute and keep trusted, and a decryption policy to maintain.

steps.title: The hook avoids all of it
steps.what: The agent hands the event to its own hook before anything is sent. There is no certificate to trust and no decryption.

steps.title: The gateway decides
steps.what: Same gateway, same policies, same detection as LLM and MCP traffic.

steps.title: The answer returns to the agent
Where it stops
steps.what: A hook only covers agents it is installed into. An agent that is not on the list is not covered, which is why the endpoint sensor still looks for the ones that are not. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.
